# 1. Core Principles of High Performance HMI

The ANSI/ISA-101.01 standard defines visual design criteria aimed at maximizing operator situational awareness, minimizing reaction time, and preventing alarm fatigue.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Rule #1: Color Reserved for Abnormal Conditions
The background must remain a muted, neutral dark/gray (#000000 or #111722). High-chroma saturated colors (Red, Amber, Yellow) are strictly reserved for active alarms and emergency states.
:::

# 2. HMI Hierarchy Levels

```
Level 1: Enterprise Overview (Macro KPIs, Plant-wide status)
  └─ Level 2: Unit Process Graphic (P&ID Operational View)
       └─ Level 3: Equipment Detail / Faceplates (PID Controllers, Tuning)
            └─ Level 4: Diagnostic & Maintenance Displays
```

# 3. Visual Element Specifications

| Element | Standard Style | Anti-Pattern (Prohibited) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Piping & Vessels** | Low-contrast gray outlines (`#2a3441`) | 3D gradients, realistic shading |
| **Active Pumps/Valves** | Static outline icon + status text | Animated rotating impellers / flames |
| **Alarm High (AH)** | Solid Amber/Yellow badge (`#ffd600`) | Flashing neon bright text |
| **Alarm High-High (AHH)**| Solid Red badge (`#ff1744`) | Screen-shaking popups |

# 4. Color Palette Tokens

```css
:root {
    --bg-main: #000000;         /* Level 1/2 Screen Background */
    --bg-panel: #111722;        /* Process Card Backdrop */
    --border-muted: #2a3441;    /* Vessel & Pipe Outlines */
    --text-primary: #e0e0e0;    /* Process Measurements (PV) */
    --color-alarm-warn: #ffd600;/* Warning / Alarm Low/High */
    --color-alarm-crit: #ff1744;/* Emergency Trip / Alarm HH */
}
```
